18125440909774239.title: Plain Water: Sludge
18125440909774239.summary: A plant does not make dirt disappear, it gathers it into one heap. That heap is almost all water, and it can eat half the running costs.

18620055217015594.title: Thirsty Industries: Food & beverage
18620055217015594.summary: Europe's biggest manufacturing sector, and most of the water it uses never touches the food. It goes on cleaning.

18400787683089630.title: Thirsty: Paper
18400787683089630.summary: About 10 litres of water per sheet, and most of it went through a tree. One ream is 5,000 litres.

18181823026415418.title: COD, in plain words
18181823026415418.summary: The number the water industry uses to measure how dirty water really is. It explains why milk in a river is a disaster.

18007999220957420.title: Thirsty: Bread
18007999220957420.summary: One kilo of bread carries about 1,608 litres of water. Almost all of it is the wheat.

17900409954552854.title: Thirsty: Milk
17900409954552854.summary: A litre of milk takes about 1,020 litres of water, and most of it feeds the cow, not the bottle.

17913231174440590.title: After you flush
17913231174440590.summary: The journey nobody watches: where your water really goes after it leaves your home.

18549367153078079.title: The plant next to the factory
18549367153078079.summary: Next to almost every serious factory there is a small water treatment plant, working around the clock.

18085403828259574.title: Thirsty: Rice
18085403828259574.summary: A flooded paddy looks like the crop must drink enormously. The real story of rice and water is stranger.

18207593962363702.title: The turn
18207593962363702.summary: Every number posted so far was spent before things reached you. From here, the story turns to the fixes.

17992220735824354.title: Thirsty: Beef
17992220735824354.summary: A 200 g steak carries about 3,100 litres of water before it reaches your plate.

17925665172399816.title: Thirsty: Chocolate
17925665172399816.summary: A 100 g bar takes about 1,700 litres, and nearly all of it falls on the cocoa farm.

18386584417162699.title: Thirsty Industries: Textile
18386584417162699.summary: Fashion withdraws 93 billion cubic metres of water a year. Here is where it goes.

18086076170650680.title: Thirsty: Jeans
18086076170650680.summary: About 8,000 litres for one pair. Even the CEO of Levi's says wash them less.

18101420441590944.title: Thirsty: T-shirt
18101420441590944.summary: A sea in Central Asia mostly turned to desert to grow cotton, and part of the reason is hanging in your wardrobe.

18144290800555765.title: Thirsty: Coffee
18144290800555765.summary: One cup of coffee drinks about 140 litres before you do.

17900627526491180.title: The 0.3%
17900627526491180.summary: Of all the water on the blue planet, what we can actually reach and use is about 0.3%.

18098046395006048.title: Thirsty Places: Singapore
18098046395006048.summary: The country that decided to drink its own wastewater, and made it a point of pride.

18347969767222892.title: Thirsty: Beer
18347969767222892.summary: One 250 ml glass takes about 74 litres, and almost none of it is spent at the brewery.

18161241001480594.title: Myth: Bottled water
18161241001480594.summary: Everyone says bottled is cleaner than tap. We test the claim with real numbers.

17982310641049220.title: Plain Water: Wastewater
17982310641049220.summary: It is not another word for sewage. Typical municipal wastewater is about 99% plain water.

17898889845356361.title: The water you can't see
17898889845356361.summary: You drank about two litres today and used more than ten thousand. Here is where they went.
